text.p: These are the headlines for selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Low-tax era on way, Paul Martin says: Finance Minister counters steady fire over Canada Pension Plan increases of 69 percent.
- Deng's death overshadowed by rights record: Supreme ruler's economic reform spawned China into a superpower.
- Possible abuse case at Gardens widens: Police receive flood of calls.
- Liberals defend sharp-tongued Young: Hurling insults at political opponents nothing new for Defence Minister.
- Health appointment under review: Tobacco spokesman's affiliation with hospital board queried.
- Orders soar for Canadair jet: Bombardier lines up C$1.5 billion in deals for new stretch version, brings in more partners.
- Tobacco sponsor limits delayed: Restrictions not expected for a year.
- Bre-X doubles Busang estimate: Insiders sold before setbacks sank stock.
- Business likes Martin's budget but C$ falls anyway.

- Bre-X weighs Busang sale: For right price it would sell 45 percent stake in Indonesian gold find, a play it says maay contain 200 million ounces of gold - 129 million ounces more than recent estimates.
